w:r.w:t: This document is based on the normalized ERD in [normalized-erd.md](/abs/path/c:
/xampp/htdocs/new_anitech/docs/normalized-erd.md). It presents each conceptual table with its fields, inferred data types, constraints, and descriptions in a presentation-friendly format.
- data types are generalized for documentation purposes
- `datetime` is used for timestamps with date and time
Table 3.5.1 presents the users table, which stores the account information of system users. It contains the basic authentication and account status details needed to manage access to the system.
Unique identifier of the user account.
Current account status of the user.

Table 3.5.2 presents the office_profiles table, which stores the personal and employment details of office personnel linked to a user account. It separates staff identity information from the authentication data kept in the users table.
Unique identifier of the office profile.
Reference to the office-side user account.
First name of the office personnel.
Middle name of the office personnel.
Last name of the office personnel.
Name suffix such as Jr. or Sr.
Employee identifier assigned to the office user.
Position or designation of the office user.
Contact number of the office user.
Table 3.5.3 presents the barangays table, which stores the master list of barangays used by the system. It serves as a reference for farmer and association location records.
Optional code used to identify the barangay.
Current status of the barangay record.
Table 3.5.4 presents the associations table, which stores the master list of farmer associations. It links associations to barangays when applicable and supports farmer grouping in the registry.
Reference to the barangay where the association belongs.
Optional code used to identify the association.
Current status of the association record.
Table 3.5.5 presents the member_types table, which stores the membership classifications used for farmers. It defines the membership rules and eligibility flags applied throughout the system.
Unique identifier of the member type.
Short code for the membership classification.
Indicates whether the type is for new members.
Indicates whether the type applies to senior members.
Indicates whether a membership fee is required.
Indicates whether members of this type are eligible for mortuary benefits.

Table 3.5.6 presents the farmers table, which stores the main registry and membership-tracking record for each farmer. It keeps only registry and membership status information, while personal profile details are stored separately.
Unique identifier of the farmer record.
Reference to the farmer's membership type.
Current overall status of the farmer record.
Current membership standing of the farmer.
Source of how the farmer record was created.
Indicates whether the record belongs to the official registry.
Date and time when the farmer was registered.
Date and time when the membership became active.
Most recent year the farmer renewed membership.
Date and time when the farmer became inactive.
Reason why the farmer became inactive.

Table 3.5.7 presents the farmer_profiles table, which stores the personal identity and contact details of each farmer. It supports normalization by separating profile data from the main farmer registry record.
Unique identifier of the farmer profile.
Reference to the farmer registry record.
Name suffix such as Jr. or Sr.
Mobile contact number of the farmer.

Table 3.5.8 presents the membership_applications table, which stores new membership application transactions submitted by farmers. It records submission, review, approval, and rejection details for the application process.
Unique identifier of the membership application.
Reference to the farmer who submitted the application.
Unique application number for the transaction.
Current processing status of the application.
Date and time when the application was submitted.
Date and time when the application was reviewed.
Date and time when the application was approved.
Short reason for rejection if the application was denied.

Table 3.5.9 presents the renewal_requests table, which stores the annual membership renewal transactions of farmers. It tracks the membership year, review details, approval details, and late renewal status.
Unique identifier of the renewal request.
Reference to the farmer requesting renewal.
Current processing status of the renewal.
Date and time when the renewal was submitted.
User who reviewed the renewal request.
Date and time when the renewal was reviewed.
Date and time when the renewal was approved.
Indicates whether the renewal was submitted late.
Additional remarks about the renewal request.

Table 3.5.10 presents the reactivation_requests table, which stores requests from inactive farmers who want to restore their membership status. It records the reason for reactivation and the review outcome.
Unique identifier of the reactivation request.
Reference to the farmer requesting reactivation.
Current processing status of the reactivation request.
Date and time when the request was submitted.
Date and time when the request was reviewed.
Additional remarks about the reactivation request.

Table 3.5.11 presents the document_requirements table, which stores the rules for required documents by workflow and submission source. It standardizes the document checklist used in membership-related transactions.
Unique identifier of the document requirement rule.
unique with source and document_type, not null
Workflow where the document is required.
unique with workflow and document_type, nullable
Optional submission source the rule applies to.
unique with workflow and source, not null
Indicates whether the rule is currently active.
Display or processing order of the requirement.

Table 3.5.12 presents the farmer_documents table, which stores the submitted documents attached to membership applications and renewal requests. It records whether required documents were received and verified by office personnel.
Unique identifier of the submitted document record.
Reference to the related membership application.
Reference to the related renewal request.
Type of document submitted or required.
Original filename of the uploaded document.
Indicates whether the document is required.
Indicates whether the document has been received.
User who marked the document as received.
Current verification status of the document.
Date and time when the document was verified.

Table 3.5.13 presents the fee_schedules table, which stores the yearly fee configuration used by the system. It defines the membership, annual, and mortuary fee amounts together with the effective dates.
Unique identifier of the fee schedule.
Membership year covered by the fee schedule.
Membership fee amount for the year.
Annual due amount for the year.
Mortuary fee amount for the year.
Indicates whether the schedule is currently active.
Date when the fee schedule takes effect.
Date when the fee schedule stops being effective.

Table 3.5.14 presents the payment_assessments table, which stores the computed payment obligations for membership applications and renewals. It captures the fee schedule used and the total amount due for the transaction.
Unique identifier of the payment assessment.
Reference to the source membership application.
Reference to the source renewal request.
Reference to the fee schedule used for the computation.
Member type recorded at the time of assessment.
Total amount that must be paid.

Table 3.5.15 presents the payments table, which stores the actual payment transactions made under a payment assessment. It records the payment method, amount paid, verification details, and receipt reference.
Unique identifier of the payment record.
Reference to the assessment being paid.
Mode or method used for payment.
External reference number for the payment.
Date and time when the payment was made.
Date and time when the payment was verified.
Receipt number issued for the payment.

Table 3.5.16 presents the membership_ledgers table, which stores the posted yearly membership results of approved applications and renewals. It summarizes fees, payment status, and mortuary eligibility for a membership year.
Unique identifier of the membership ledger entry.
Membership year covered by the ledger entry.
Reference to the source membership application.
Reference to the source renewal request.
Member type recorded when the ledger was posted.
Membership fee posted to the ledger.
Annual due posted to the ledger.
Mortuary fee posted to the ledger.
Total amount due posted to the ledger.
Total amount paid for the ledger entry.
Date and time when the related payment was completed.
Current payment status in the ledger.
Indicates whether the ledger entry qualifies for mortuary benefits.
Current status of the ledger entry.

Table 3.5.17 presents the mortuary_claims table, which stores the mortuary benefit claims filed against eligible membership ledger entries. It records the claim details, supporting document status, and office action references.
Unique identifier of the mortuary claim.
Reference to the eligible membership ledger entry.
Unique reference number for the claim.
Amount claimed under the mortuary benefit.
Date the claim was filed or recorded.
Name of the person claiming the benefit.
Relationship of the claimer to the deceased member.
Indicates whether the claimer's valid ID was received.
Indicates whether proof of relationship was received.
Indicates whether the death certificate was received.
Current processing status of the claim.
User who filed the claim record in the system.
Table 3.5.18 presents the advisories table, which stores announcements published for specific audiences. It supports targeting by barangay, association, and publication status.
Title of the advisory or announcement.
URL-friendly unique identifier of the advisory.
Current publication status of the advisory.
Target audience category of the advisory.
Reference to the targeted barangay when applicable.
Reference to the targeted association when applicable.
Date and time when the advisory was published.
Table 3.5.19 presents the advisory_attachments table, which stores files attached to advisories. It supports the distribution of supplementary documents together with announcements.
Unique identifier of the advisory attachment.
Reference to the advisory that owns the attachment.
Original filename of the attached file.

Table 3.5.20 presents the advisory_member_type table, which stores the bridge records for advisory targeting by member type. It enables many-to-many filtering between advisories and membership classifications.
Unique identifier of the bridge record.
FK -> advisories.id, unique with member_type_id, not null
FK -> member_types.id, unique with advisory_id, not null
Reference to the targeted member type.
Table 3.5.21 presents the queries table, which stores farmer-submitted concerns and inquiries. It tracks the subject, status, and archival state of each query.
Unique identifier of the farmer query.
Reference to the farmer who submitted the query.
Subject or topic of the query.
Date and time when the query was archived.
Table 3.5.22 presents the query_images table, which stores image attachments submitted with farmer queries. It keeps the uploaded file references associated with each query.
Unique identifier of the query image.
Reference to the query that owns the image.
Original filename of the uploaded image.
Table 3.5.23 presents the query_responses table, which stores the responses given by office personnel to farmer queries. It records the responder and the response message for each inquiry.
Unique identifier of the query response.
Reference to the query being answered.
User who responded to the query.
Response message sent for the query.
Table 3.5.24 presents the query_response_attachments table, which stores files attached to query responses. It supports sending supporting documents together with an office reply.
Unique identifier of the query response attachment.
Reference to the query response that owns the attachment.
Original filename of the attached file.
- `users` now stores only account-level data and no longer carries farmer identity fields or a direct `farmer_id`.
- `office_profiles` now contains the personal identity fields for office personnel.
- `farmers` now stores only registry and membership-tracking data.
- `farmer_profiles` is added as a separate one-to-one table for farmer identity and contact details.
- Direct source or circular references removed in the normalized ERD are also omitted here.
